subtype: Approach: family code word as a test [Action]
passage:
Papa had said it at breakfast: no word, no going.
"Yamini? Your father sent me to pick you up," the man said at the school gate.
Yamini stayed where she was. "What's the word?"
"The word?"
"Our family word. Only people Papa trusts know it."
"He didn't tell me any word. Come on, we'll be late."
"Then I'm not coming." She turned to the watchman. "Joseph Uncle, please call my father?"
"Fine, forget it," the man muttered, and walked off.
"Good girl," said Joseph Uncle. "Sit by my cabin. I'm calling him right now."

qa.q: Who does Yamini ask to call her father?
qa.a: She asks Joseph Uncle, the watchman.

qa.q: What was Yamini feeling when the man could not give the word?
qa.a: Wary and firm, since she refused to go and turned to the watchman for help.

qa.q: What else could Yamini's family add to keep pick-ups safe, and why?
qa.a: They could agree that Yamini phones her father to confirm any pick-up, which gives a second check besides the word.

qa.q: How does Joseph Uncle see Yamini's question about the word?
qa.a: Joseph Uncle sees a sensible child following a family plan, so he praises her and phones her father at once.

grounding: A family code word lets a girl test a man claiming her father sent him, and she leaves when he cannot give it.

subtype: Approach: family code word as a test [Action]
passage: At home we have a secret word. Only Ammi, Abbu, my Khala and my grandfather know it. Ammi said, "If anyone else says they've come to fetch you, ask for the word." Last month, after school, a man walked up to me at the gate. "Your Abbu sent me. He's busy. Come." My hands went sweaty. I said, "What's the word?" He looked confused. "What word?" I said, "Then I'm not coming," and walked right back into school, to our class teacher. She kept me in the staffroom and called Abbu, who came himself and hugged me for a long time. He said, "Nazia, my beti, you did exactly right." That night he told the police and the school.

qa.q: Who knows the family's secret word?
qa.a: Ammi, Abbu, Khala and the grandfather.

qa.q: How did Nazia feel when the man said Abbu had sent him?
qa.a: Nazia felt nervous, with sweaty hands, but stayed firm enough to ask for the word.

qa.q: What else could Nazia's family do to keep the code word working?
qa.a: They could change it if anyone outside the family learns it, so it stays a real test.

qa.q: How does the moment look to Abbu?
qa.a: Abbu is shaken and relieved, hugging Nazia for a long time, and reports it to the police and school that night.

grounding: It shows a child using the family's secret code word to test a man claiming her father sent him, and leaving when he cannot say it.

subtype: Approach: family code word as a test [Action]
passage:
Class teacher's note, Tuesday
At dismissal today, a man I did not know approached Vishakha at the gate and said her father had sent him to collect her. From across the yard I saw her stop and ask him something. Later she told me she had asked for the family's code word. He could not say it. She turned at once and walked straight back to me, calm but pale. I kept her with me in the classroom, called her father, and informed the principal, who has contacted the police. Her father came within twenty minutes. Vishakha told him, "I asked for the word, and he didn't know it." I have asked for the code word idea to be shared with all parents.
- Kiran

qa.q: Who did Vishakha walk back to after the man could not say the word?
qa.a: She walked straight back to the class teacher.

qa.q: How was Vishakha feeling when she walked back?
qa.a: She looked calm but pale, so she was probably frightened but in control.

qa.q: What else could the school do to protect all children at dismissal?
qa.a: The school could require a named pick-up list at the gate, checked by staff, so strangers are stopped earlier.

qa.q: How does the day look to Vishakha's father?
qa.a: Her father is likely shaken and proud, hearing that she used the code word and walked away.

grounding: It shows a child using a family code word to test a man who claimed her father sent him, and leaving when he could not give it.
